subject: Model identification for unidimensional and bifactor models

messages.author: 52cba7e2a806f86f
messages.subject: Model identification for unidimensional and bifactor models
parts:
Dear Phil,

I found from your package manual as well as earlier discussion in this forum that, for unidimensional IRT models, you fix the mean of theta to 0 and variance of theta to 1 for identification purposes. I was hoping to utilize this feature to apply the "equivalent group linking" concept across a few calibrations --- Because the response data of the calibrations are from the same group of respondents, when the mean and standard deviation of theta are held constant, the item parameters are on the same scale. 

However, when I tried to double check by computing theta through fscores() and looking at their mean and standard deviation, they are quite different from 0 and 1. Sometimes I have a mean of 0.3, or a standard deviation of .6 or 1.3, even when I used method = "ML". I wonder why they are not close to 0 and 1?

I also tried to look at the theta distribution from fitting a bifactor model. The mean and standard deviation for neither the general factor nor the specific factors were close to 0 and 1. Are we suppose to have all the thetas on the general factor and the specific factors standardized?

Thank you very much for your help!
Yi Zheng
Arizona State University
